extracted.intended_audience: donors, members of the public, and people living with diabetes interested in Diabetes UK-funded research (also useful to researchers seeking Diabetes UK funding)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and expectations Diabetes UK communicates for the research projects it funds or lists, including how projects are reviewed, approved, presented to donors, and what metadata and status labels they carry. The page is donor-facing and emphasizes scientific quality, patient involvement, investigator capability, relevance/impact, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: World-class diabetes research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organisation states it supports around 120 research projects across the UK; projects are presented as being of the highest scientific quality and are only possible thanks to donors and supporters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert review
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every research project is reviewed by experts"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects undergo expert scientific review prior to funding/listing. This is stated as part of Diabetes UK's process for ensuring scientific quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval by research committee
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded/listed projects receive formal approval from Diabetes UK's research committee as part of governance and selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval by panel of people living with diabetes (public/patient involvement)
rubrics_metrics.description: "approved by ... our panel of people living with diabetes"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects are additionally reviewed/approved by a panel made up of people living with diabetes, indicating an explicit requirement for lay/patient involvement in project approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator capability: led by researchers with appropriate skills and experience
rubrics_metrics.description: "led by researchers with the skills and experience to succeed"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diabetes UK highlights investigator qualifications and track record as a criterion for supporting projects, emphasizing likelihood of successful delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance and impact: tackling complications and moving towards a cure
rubrics_metrics.description: "Your support of our research projects means we can keep tackling the complications of diabetes and bring us one step closer to a cure."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects are framed and evaluated for their potential to address diabetes complications, prevention, remission, treatments, or progress toward a cure — impact and relevance to people with diabetes are central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Donor-facing transparency: project pages must showcase research details
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each project page showcases the details of the research, and if you find a research project you could really get behind, you can support it in lots of different ways."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project listings are expected to provide summaries and clear information so donors can choose projects to support; transparency and accessible summaries are part of how projects are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project metadata and tagging (diabetes type, region, topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings include "Tags" such as Type 1, Type 2, Complications, Prevention, Remission, region labels (e.g., Northern Ireland, South West), and thematic tags (e.g., Healthcare, Innovation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects are categorized with structured metadata (disease type, region, topic) to enable searching and filtering; these metadata fields are part of how projects are described and discoverable by stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project adoption / status labelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Status shown as e.g. "Project available for adoption" or "Project not available for adoption"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each project includes a clear status indicating whether it can currently be adopted or supported by donors (linked to the "Donate to a discovery" scheme); status is a procedural quality/availability indicator presented to users.
